# Agent notes

## Project

- Upstream repository: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode
- OpenCode GUI plugin documentation: https://opencode.ai/docs/build/plugins/gui/
- This project targets OpenCode v2.

## Commands

- `bun run check` — canonical verification (`tsc --noEmit`). Never run `tsc` with other flags.
- `bun test` — tests are colocated (`*.test.ts` beside sources), pure logic only: no network, no mocks.
- `bun run build` / `bun run watch` — the GUI bundle (`dist/gui-experimental.cjs`). The server part is
  loaded as TypeScript source; it is never built.

## Architecture rules

- `src/model.ts`, `src/rpc.ts`, `src/associate.ts`, `src/extract.ts` (core), and everything in `src/gui/`
  must stay provider-agnostic: generic kinds (`issue | pr | run`), statuses, repo slugs, and provider
  ids/marks resolved through registries. Never import a provider's network module from the GUI.
- Provider-specific code lives only in `src/providers/<name>/` (server: auth, hydration, merge settings,
  branch runs) and its lexicon (pure, bundled into windows).
- The RPC contract (`src/rpc.ts`) is the only shared runtime token between the two runtimes. Zod schemas
  there define the shapes; keep `src/model.ts` types aligned with them (zod infers mutable arrays).
- Effect `Schema` is not a dependency here; validation is zod via Standard Schema.

## Style

- `const` over `let`; early returns over `else`; no `try`/`catch` except at genuine environment
  boundaries (git subprocess, network, integration APIs).
- No `any`. Type inference over annotations; annotate only exports and literal-widening spots.
- Tests: one `describe` per function, table-ish cases, assert exact shapes.
- Commits: conventional (`feat:`, `fix:`, `docs:`, `chore:`…), no scope unless clarifying.

name: session-debug
description: Inspect an OpenCode v2 session's storage and messages (opencode.db SQLite) and trace why Muninn's pill/footer shows a given issue, PR, or run. Triggers on "why is X in this session", debug-footer questions, ref-provenance questions, and session-data forensics.

# Session Debug

Debug "why does Muninn show X" from the outside in: find the session, dump its
messages, replay the extraction pipeline, verify hydration. V2 storage only.

## 1. Storage: one SQLite DB, not JSON files

Everything lives in `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` (WAL mode). The old
`storage/` tree holds pre-v2 rows — ignore it. Inspect read-only; never write.

```sh
sqlite3 -readonly ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db "<query>"
```

Table map:

| Table            | Contents                                                                                                  |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `session_v2`     | Current sessions: `id` (`ses_…`), `directory`, `title`, `project_id`, timestamps                          |
| `session_message`| One row per message: `id` (`msg_…`), `session_id`, `type` (`user`/`assistant`/`system`/`idle`), `seq`, `data` JSON |
| `blob`/`blob_ref`| Content-addressed blobs (images, attachments) referenced from message data                                |

Gotcha: `session`, `message`, `part`, and `session_part` exist but hold legacy
or empty data for v2 sessions. The **whole message — including the assistant
`content[]` parts — is inlined in `session_message.data`**. Don't hunt for a
parts table.

## 2. Recipes

The debug footer carries the full session ID (`gate ✓ <sessionID>`); `LIKE '<prefix>%'` works when you only have part of it:

```sh
sqlite3 -readonly ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db \
  "SELECT id, directory, title FROM session_v2 WHERE id LIKE 'ses_e41ec%'"
```

Dump the conversation in order (this is exactly what the GUI scans via
`session.message.list`):

```sh
out=$(mktemp) && sqlite3 -readonly ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db \
  "SELECT data FROM session_message WHERE session_id='<id>' ORDER BY seq" > "$out"
```

Transcripts can contain secrets (tokens, auth headers in tool output):
`mktemp` creates the file 0600 — keep it that way, redact before sharing, and
`rm "$out"` when done.

Message shapes (what each `data` JSON contains):

- `user`: `text` (what Muninn's user bucket scans) + `metadata.displayText`
- `assistant`: `content[]` of parts — `{type: "text" | "reasoning", text}` and
  `{type: "tool", tool?, state}` where `state` has `status`, `input`
  (`command`, `path`, …), and `content[]` of `{type: "text", text}` blocks
- `system` / `idle`: no scannable text

Only `state.status === "completed"` tool parts count — `messageBuckets` skips
the rest.

## 3. Replay the pipeline (src/extract.ts)

Port these functions to any language (Python is fine) and run them over the
dump to attribute each ref to its bucket, message, and exact match:

1. `stripCode` — remove fenced blocks and inline spans first.
2. `scan` — lexicon URLs/shorthand (src/providers/github/lexicon.ts), kind
   words, bare hashes; session repo is the session directory's git remote.
3. `messageBuckets` — user / commands (`state.input.command`) / prose
   (text+reasoning) / outputs (`state.content[]` text blocks, grouped per tool
   call).
4. `deliberateRefs` — tier rank user < command < prose < output (a ref keeps
   its best tier); **each text block of a tool output is judged on its own**:
   a block naming ≥ `LISTING_THRESHOLD` (3) refs of one kind is a listing and
   that kind drops from that block. Three blocks with one PR each keep all
   three.

Validate the simulation by asserting the debug footer's census matches
(`refs N (user a cmd b prose c out d)`). Then check hydration upstream:

```sh
gh pr view <n> --repo <owner>/<repo> --json state,title,updatedAt,headRefName
gh issue view <n> --repo <owner>/<repo> --json state,title
```

A ref "in the session" without an entity in the store is **not** automatically
a hydration failure. It can be:

- *pending* — the debounced message-change hydration hasn't run yet; re-check
- *skipped* — never sent to a provider: an unsupported ref host falls back to
  the session's own provider, so a ref drops silently only when neither
  resolves (no repo for the ref, no forge remote for the session) — these
  never count as unresolved
- *unresolved* — the provider was asked and returned nothing: wrong number,
  deleted run, private repo without a credential

## 4. Reading the debug footer

Built by `debugLine` in src/gui/window.tsx:

```
mn gui <sha+time> · srv <sha> · gate ✓ <sessionID> · chains N · eligible N
· pill: <#n title> · pick: <danger|newest|runs-only|none>[ of M] · lead <branch match|newest|—>
· refs N (user a cmd b prose c out d) → hits H/E ents[ · err <step>]
· SENT[/TOTAL] refs → H hydrated (kinds) · U unresolved[ (#nums)][ · K invalid dropped]
```

- `gate ✓` — the mounted session matches the pill's session (else pills are off)
- `pick` — `pillPick` rule that won: `danger` / `newest` / `runs-only` /
  `none`; `of M` counts PR chains for PR picks, run-bearing chains for
  `runs-only`;
  `lead` says whether the chain's lead PR matched the session's checkout branch
  (`branch match`) or is just the most recent (`—` for run-only picks, which
  print `run #id`; `pick: none` omits the lead part entirely)
- `refs` census — extracted candidates by provenance tier; `out` = tool outputs
- `hits/E` — how many refs hit the durable entity store of E cached entities
- `hydrated` / `unresolved` — outcome of the last **refresh-cycle** hydration
  (session mount or 30s poll). The debounced hydration on message changes
  updates `unresolved` but not the stats line, so stats can lag the newest
  messages. Unresolved = the provider was asked and returned nothing (wrong
  number, deleted run, private repo without a credential); refs skipped before
  hydration never appear here. `SENT/TOTAL` appears when `wireRefs` drops
  invalid refs or caps the payload at 64 (most deliberate tiers first);
  `K invalid dropped` counts refs whose numbers fail the wire contract (a
  prose `#0`) — before `wireRefs` existed, one such ref rejected the whole
  hydrate RPC and wedged the panel error on
- `err <step>` — the last refresh failure's step (`repo` / `hydrate` /
  `branch-runs`); the panel shows the full `step: message` line. The server
  swallows provider errors into `unresolved`, so an error here is almost
  always transport (server restart) or an RPC contract rejection — check the
  browser console for `[muninn] <step> failed`

## 5. Known false-positive families (fixed on this branch — shapes still useful)

- Line-numbered tool output used to fabricate refs: a kind word at end of line
  plus the next line's number (`…via-pr\n6:`) scanned as `PR 6`; inline-code
  spans stripped by `stripCode` did the same for `run` (see the scan test "kind
  words and their numbers must share a line"). The shapes still explain phantom
  entities in older durable-cache entries and old debug footers.
- Coincidental collisions hydrate: a fabricated number can resolve to a real,
  unrelated entity (hydrated ≠ deliberate).
- The pill pick now runs over eligible chains only, and `pillPick` never returns a
  chain lacking both PRs and runs — a dead (merged) chain can't win, and an
  issue-only chain renders no pill at all.

# muninn

Named for Odin's raven of memory — it remembers what an OpenCode session ships.

Tracks what an OpenCode session ships: pull requests, issues, and CI runs —
extracted from the conversation, hydrated from the forge, and shown live in
OpenCode Desktop.

## Decision models

Conversation extraction can find references that were only mentioned in passing.
When enabled, a decision model evaluates each candidate in context and estimates
whether it is important enough to keep in Muninn's pill and sidebar; this helps
filter incidental references without losing items that matter to the session.
Select a backend and model in Muninn's settings. Requests use credentials
already connected to OpenCode.

## Add the plugin

Install the plugin directly from its GitHub repository with OpenCode's plugin
manager. OpenCode documents the `github:owner/repo` form for `plugin add` in its
[plugin docs](https://opencode.ai/docs/plugins/#manage):

```sh
opencode plugin add github:esafak/muninn
```

To test a pull request before it merges, install its branch the same way:

```sh
opencode plugin add github:esafak/muninn#docs/readme-screenshots-settings-audit
```

Branches, tags, and full commit hashes all work.

For development and contributor guidance, see [CONTRIBUTORS.md](CONTRIBUTORS.md).

# Contributor guide

Development notes for contributors to Muninn. User-facing setup and usage are
in [README.md](README.md).

## Development commands

- `bun install` — install dependencies.
- `bun test` — run colocated pure-logic tests (`*.test.ts`); tests do not use
  network access or mocks.
- `bun run check` — canonical verification (`tsc --noEmit`). Do not run `tsc`
  with other flags.
- `bun run build` / `bun run watch` — build or watch the GUI bundle at
  `dist/gui-experimental.cjs`. The server is loaded as TypeScript source and is
  not built.

## Load a local checkout

To develop against this checkout in OpenCode Desktop, add its absolute
directory path to the `plugins` array in the global config at
`~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc`:

```jsonc
{
  "plugins": ["/absolute/path/to/muninn"]
}
```

Replace the example with this checkout's path. If you installed Muninn from
GitHub, replace that plugin entry with the local path rather than loading both.
Run `bun run watch` to rebuild the GUI bundle; each rebuild reloads the GUI in
every window. Server source changes require restarting the server.

## Architecture

- Package exports: `.` is the OpenCode server plugin, `./rpc` is the shared
  contract, and `./gui-experimental` is the prebuilt desktop-window bundle.
  The server resolves repositories from `git remote`, hydrates references, and
  applies merge policy through the Muninn RPC. GitHub REST uses integration
  credentials, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, or anonymous access for public repositories.
- `src/model.ts`, `src/rpc.ts`, `src/associate.ts`, `src/extract.ts` (core), and
  everything in `src/gui/` must remain provider-agnostic: generic kinds
  (`issue | pr | run`), statuses, repo slugs, and provider IDs/marks resolved
  through registries. Never import a provider's network module from the GUI.
- Provider-specific code belongs in `src/providers/<name>/`: server-side auth,
  hydration, merge settings, branch runs, and a pure lexicon bundled into
  windows.
- `src/rpc.ts` is the only shared runtime contract. Keep `src/model.ts` aligned
  with its Zod schemas (which infer mutable arrays).
- Validation uses Zod via Standard Schema; Effect `Schema` is not a dependency.

## Providers

The provider seam is `src/providers/types.ts`. The GUI renders generic kinds
(`issue | pr | run`), statuses, and repo slugs, never provider-specific data.
Provider lexicons (URL and shorthand patterns for session scanning) and product
marks are pure and bundled into windows; auth, hydration, merge settings, and
branch runs are server-side and dispatched by claimed host.

To add a provider, implement `SourceProvider` and a lexicon, register both, and
extend the `ProviderID` union. No UI changes should be needed.

## Style

- Prefer `const` and early returns. Use `try`/`catch` only at genuine environment
  boundaries (git subprocesses, network, integration APIs).
- Avoid `any`; prefer inference, annotating exports and literal-widening spots.
- Tests: one `describe` per function, table-like cases, and exact-shape asserts.
- Commits use conventional prefixes (`feat:`, `fix:`, `docs:`, `chore:`…),
  without a scope unless it clarifies.
